comparison: Both strongly support the identification of promiscuous substrate activities in wild-type transporters (C45-C60, C142). OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design and statistical significance, while peer reviewers praise the methodology as 'well thought through' and acknowledge this as a key contribution. High agreement on these findings.

Both support the site-directed mutagenesis findings showing single mutations enhance substrate transport (C84-C91). OpenEval highlights the correlation between growth and uptake data, while peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'faster growth on the said amino acids was confirmed' and validated by uptake experiments. Strong concordance.

Both support the PUT4-S mutation findings (C94-C96). OpenEval emphasizes the independent recovery from two selection conditions, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'single mutants are identified that modulate substrate specificity.' Agreement on the gain-of-function for glutamate transport.

Both strongly support the key finding that evolved transporters retain original substrate activities while gaining new ones (C99-C113, C132-C133, C167-C169, C191-C192). OpenEval details the statistical methods and fitness landscape analysis, while peer reviewers emphasize this validates the generalist intermediate model. This represents a central conclusion with unanimous support.

Overlapping support for fitness trade-off characterization. OpenEval R4 covers comprehensive fitness measurements (C99-C113, C167-C169, C191-C192), while peer R5 focuses on the observation that some variants show diminished capacity on original substrates (C100-C105, C110-C113, C168-C169, C191-C192). Both accept the trade-off findings.

Both support the correlation between uptake rates and growth rates (C114-C119 in OpenEval, C114-C118, C123 in peer review). OpenEval notes the use of two substrate concentrations strengthens conclusions, while peer reviewers explicitly validate that 'correlation plots show that the assays based on growth rates versus radioactive uptake assays indeed can explain the effect of the mutations to a large extent.'

Partial overlap on fitness characterization. OpenEval R6 addresses PUT4-S fitness and uptake correlations (C121-C131, C134), while peer R5 covers broader fitness trade-offs including some overlapping claims (C121-C122). Both support the findings but focus on different aspects of the fitness landscape.

Perfect agreement on the dramatic substrate range expansion by L207S mutation (C135-C138). OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive growth assays and mechanistic insights from substrate property analysis, while peer reviewers acknowledge this demonstrates how 'gain-of-function mutations also confer transport promiscuity, expanding the range of amino acids transported.'

Both support the convergent evolution findings and structural analysis (C71-C83). OpenEval emphasizes the convergent recovery of L207S and structural predictions, while peer reviewers validate the evolution experiments as providing 'convincing evidence' and note 'the data appear accurate.' Strong concordance on the evolutionary methodology and findings.

Both support the experimental evolution methodology (C62-C70). OpenEval validates the OrthoRep system design and mutation coverage, while peer reviewers state the manuscript 'provides convincing evidence' for the evolution experiments and confirm the data accuracy. Agreement on methodological soundness.

Strong agreement on the main evolutionary conclusions (C36, C188-C190, C201). OpenEval states these are well-supported by experimental data showing evolution through generalist intermediates, while peer reviewers unanimously endorse this, with Reviewer 1 stating findings 'provide convincing evidence' and Reviewer 3 confirming 'the data in the paper support the conclusions.'

Perfect agreement on surface expression controls (C92-C93, C97-C98). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support these controls as ruling out expression differences. Peer Reviewer 2 specifically acknowledges 'The authors performed experiments as part of the revision to show that the studied mutations do not greatly change surface expression of the transporters.'

Both rate these claims as UNCERTAIN (C108-C109, C120). OpenEval notes these are speculative interpretations requiring additional experiments to confirm, while peer reviewers do not directly address this specific mechanistic interpretation. Agreement that the mistargeting hypothesis remains uncertain despite supporting microscopy data.

Both rate the plasmid copy number hypothesis as UNCERTAIN (C143-C147). OpenEval notes this is a reasonable but speculative hypothesis lacking direct experimental support, while peer reviewers do not directly validate or challenge this interpretation. Agreement on uncertainty despite the assay's demonstrated sensitivity.

OpenEval supports the experimental observations about Arg/Orn exclusion and background growth limitations (C47-C49). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these represent appropriate acknowledgment of experimental limitations.

OpenEval rates speculative explanations for observed phenomena as UNCERTAIN (C55-C56, C151). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These represent plausible but untested mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations based on structural predictions as UNCERTAIN (C156-C157, C130). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. Direct structural studies would be needed to confirm these inferences.

OpenEval supports evolutionary interpretations about AGP1-G having no fitness loss on original substrates (C171-C176, C193-C194). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these claims are implicitly supported by peer acceptance of the generalist intermediate model.

OpenEval supports the contextualization and acknowledgment of limitations in generalizing to natural evolution (C177-C182). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'make careful conclusions saying that in real life, the evolutionary landscape is way more complex.'

Partial overlap on background knowledge and literature context. OpenEval R19 covers extensive background claims (C1-C44, C140-C141, C195-C200), while peer R1 includes some overlapping background claims (C6, C147, C198). Both support the appropriateness of the conceptual framework.

Partial overlap on evolutionary theory context. OpenEval R19 includes standing genetic variation discussion (C195-C200), while peer R9 addresses the main evolutionary conclusions (C199-C200). Both support the connection to broader evolutionary theory.

OpenEval supports structural and evolutionary context through comparative analysis (C153-C166). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These comparisons strengthen mechanistic interpretation through homology to characterized transporters.

OpenEval supports the use of CYN1 as a natural example of transporter specialization (C183-C187). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. This contextualizes the experimental findings within natural evolutionary processes.

OpenEval supports the placement of findings in context of prior transporter evolution work (C150). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this is implicitly validated by peer reviewers noting the study extends concepts from enzyme evolution to transporters.
